summary: The best React path. @lottiefiles/dotlottie-react 0.21.1 is active, MIT, provenance-signed, supports React 17/18/19, and plays both Lottie JSON and .lottie. A React 19 spike loaded both formats from a self-hosted WASM file in about 58 ms, with 90 frames each. The main cost is the 481 KB gzip WASM runtime and the need to self-host it for CSP or offline use.
reasoning: Active release line: 0.21.1 published 2026-11-02, with the dependency pinned exactly to @lottiefiles/dotlottie-web 0.82.1.
Peers React ^17 || ^18 || ^19, so React 18 and 19 are both covered.
MIT with a permissive runtime tree: React, React DOM, the React wrapper and the DotLottie web player are all MIT.
The npm tarball is provenance-signed and published by GitHub Actions through a trusted publisher.
The player supports .lottie and Lottie JSON through the same component; the spike loaded both formats.
No preinstall, install or postinstall script in the isolated runtime tree.
The 1.2 MB WASM (about 481 KB gzip) and 73 KB worker can be self-hosted; the spike used setWasmUrl() and a local wasm file.
The React 19 spike rendered two canvases, reported 90 frames for each format, and produced no page errors.
caveats: The WASM runtime is about 481 KB gzip and is fetched separately from the JS bundle. Budget for it and cache it.
By default the player fetches a version-pinned WASM from jsDelivr or unpkg. Self-host it with setWasmUrl() for CSP, offline or supply-chain control.
WebAssembly may require wasm-unsafe-eval in a strict CSP; the worker path needs worker-src, or a self-hosted worker via setWorkerUrl().
Browser-only. The component needs a canvas and is not a server-rendering target; use it in a client component or after mount.
React 18 was not spiked; the peer range covers it, but verify it in the consuming application if React 18 is used.
The Spike used a simple 90-frame animation; state machines, themes, audio and large .lottie assets were not exercised.

evidence.label: License
evidence.detail: MIT. The isolated runtime tree is React, React DOM, @lottiefiles/dotlottie-react and @lottiefiles/dotlottie-web, all MIT.

evidence.label: React compatibility
evidence.detail: peerDependencies react: ^17 || ^18 || ^19. The spike used React 19.2.0.

evidence.label: Format support
evidence.detail: The component accepts .lottie and .json through src, and JSON strings or .lottie ArrayBuffers through data. The spike loaded both formats.

evidence.label: Dependency footprint
evidence.detail: One exact runtime dependency, @lottiefiles/dotlottie-web 0.82.1. 15 MB installed with React, 503 KB unpacked for the wrapper itself.

evidence.label: Install scripts
evidence.detail: No preinstall, install or postinstall script in the wrapper or the isolated runtime tree.

evidence.label: TypeScript types
evidence.detail: Bundled dist/index.d.ts with typed props and re-exported DotLottie types.

evidence.label: Known advisories
evidence.detail: OSV returned no advisories for @lottiefiles/dotlottie-react@0.21.1 or @lottiefiles/dotlottie-web@0.82.1.

evidence.label: Maintenance
evidence.detail: 0.21.1 published 2026-11-02; repository pushed 2026-11-02; active, 938 stars and 21 open issues.

evidence.label: npm provenance
evidence.detail: SLSA provenance is present on 0.21.1; npm records GitHub Actions as the publisher via a trusted publisher.

evidence.label: React browser spike
evidence.detail: A Vite production build rendered .lottie and JSON side by side in Chrome 1200x800. Both canvases reached 90 frames; the page loaded in 58 ms with self-hosted WASM. The JS bundle was 356.93 KB / 93.15 KB gzip; the WASM is 481 KB gzip separately.

evidence.label: Self-hosted runtime assets
evidence.detail: The spike copied dotlottie-player.wasm and dotlottie.worker.js from the installed package and called setWasmUrl() with the local file; no CDN fetch was used.
